html:
Goguryeo was a Korean kingdom of northern Korea and southern Manchuria, from 37 BCE to 668 CE. It was the largest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea, alongside Paekche and Silla, and a short form of its name, Goryeo, gave us the word "Korea".

Tradition says the archer Jumong founded it in 37 BCE. It grew in the mountains along the Yalu River, fighting Chinese commanderies and steppe peoples, and became a hard military state of fortresses and cavalry.

Key moments:

  • 372: Buddhism arrived from China, and a Confucian academy was set up.
  • 391 to 413: King Gwanggaeto the Great pushed the borders far into Manchuria and south into the peninsula.
  • 427: King Jangsu moved the capital to Pyongyang.
  • 598 to 614: Goguryeo beat back huge invasions by the Sui dynasty, winning the Battle of Salsu in 612. The cost of these wars helped bring the Sui down.
  • 645: it held off the first Tang invasion.

The end came after the strongman Yeon Gaesomun died around 666 and his sons fought each other. A Silla and Tang alliance took Pyongyang in 668. Many of its people were moved into China. In 698 Dae Joyeong, a former Goguryeo general, founded Balhae in the north as its successor, and centuries later Goryeo took its name.
sum: Goguryeo was a Korean kingdom of northern Korea and southern Manchuria, from 37 BCE to 668 CE. It was the largest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea, alongside Paekche and Silla, and a short form of its name, Goryeo, gave us the word "Korea".
